data.turoyo: bale hənne miṯe mu kafno, ṣayome, mṣalyone w baxoye w šapərza, Aloho mhawən aʕlayye.
data.translation: Dabei waren sie halbtot vor Hunger, sie fasteten, beteten und waren in einem elenden Zustand, Gott sei ihnen gnädig.

rationale: Thin Infectum: plural ʕal-affected participant in hardship.

data.turoyo: Ya abri, ma kḥozat dukṯi? Alo mhawən aʕli, u baytayḏi ʕiqo yo w darbo layto.
data.translation: Mein Sohn, siehst du nicht, wie ich wohne? Gott, mach es mir leicht! Mein Haus ist gar eng und es gibt keine Möglichkeit.

rationale: Thin Infectum: first-person ʕal participant and intelligible housing context.

data.turoyo: lo, lo kofayšo, ma mə gfayšo, Aloho mhawan!
data.translation: Nein, es existiert nicht mehr, wie soll es noch existieren, Gott möge sich unser erbarmen!

rationale: Fills Infectum to five and preserves unusual mhawan vocalism; does not infer an encoded first-plural suffix.

summary: All fifteen records attest the established divine-help formula. God is the grammatical subject; an affected participant may be ʕal-marked or implicit. German erbarmen and help paraphrases do not establish a distinct mercy sense.

Unprefixed mhawən in a wish remains Infectum, not Imperativ. No other stem or box is warranted. Bare exclamations and participant-marked variants do not require new senses or a duplicate idiom when the entry already treats the formula as its sense.
The formula occurs in direct appeals, narrated hardship and narrator asides; this distribution shows discourse use, without proving that the verb is unavailable with other subjects.
Existing 20/14 and 95/26 are not repeated. 108/26 attests the formula and is an existing reference, but its surrounding wording differs from the current orphan example.
Jan's English is project machine translation, copied only as supplied and not used to establish senses. All interpretations were checked against the Turoyo.

Both Jan tokens continue the established Aloho mhawən invocation in food shortage or hardship. God is the grammatical subject; beneficiaries are implicit. No make-wise, new mercy meaning or independent Idiomatic phrases item is warranted.
The reader's thin-cell count of two omits three round-1 additions. The effective Infectum I.1 cell is already five; no Jan examples are added.
66/56 has a mismatched supplied translation. The reader mentions 66/57, but that translation is not supplied here; check the edition before publishing any example.
Is Talay mhawan a vowel variant of mhawən or a contraction involving a beneficiary? Do not infer first plural only from German unser.

Does the second inherited example's 108/26 reference intentionally point to an alternative formula context rather than its full orphan quotation? Confirm the team's multi-reference convention before altering it.
